headline: Approved new family authorization for interment policy; no vote taken on ISVT burial lot payment plan.
summary: The commission approved a new family authorization for interment policy. It discussed a possible payment plan and MOU for ISVT's purchase of 67 graves in Section 8, but took no formal vote on that.
decisions: Approved the family authorization for interment policy as drafted.
Commission verbally agreed to move forward with a payment plan and MOU for ISVT, if legal; no formal vote was taken.

decision_evidence.quote: Wesley moved to adopt family authorization for interment policy as drafted. McCallum and Millar-House second. The motion passes.
He will be able to tell McClenahan that the commission has verbally agreed to move forward with payment plan and MOU as long as it's legal.

decision_titles: Payment plan and MOU for ISVT lot purchase
plain_text:
Cemetery Superintendent/BPRW Director: Cindi Wight 
  Chair: Jennifer Diaz 
 Vice-chair – Alexandra Millar  
  
 
 
City of Burlington    455 North Avenue    Burlington, Vermont 05401    (802) 863-2075 
 
Cemetery Commission Meeting Minutes 
 
 
Meeting Date:  October 22, 2026 
 
Commissioners Present: Jennifer Diaz, Miles McCallum, Alexandra Millar-House, Mary Wesley (Nancy 
Kirby was not present)  
 
Staff Present: Holli Bushnell, Steve Bachand,  
 
Meeting was called to order 4:37pm at by Chair Jennifer Diaz 
 
I. Approval of Agenda 
Alexandra Millar-House moved to adopt the agenda, Diaz moved to second, all were in favor 
 
II. Approval of minutes from 6/23/2025 
Miles McCallum moved to approve the minutes, Diaz seconded, all were in favor 
 
III. Public Forum 
Public forum was opened at 4:39pm, as no one was present or wished to speak, public forum 
was also closed at 4:39pm 
 
IV. ISVT Update 
Steve Bachand shared that he has had two meetings with ISVT, including one yesterday 
(10/21/2026).  At the first meeting they discussed the future green/natural burial area in Section 
8 closest to existing Muslim section.  This was purely an informational meeting.  ISVT was 
informed at this meeting that they will need to purchase all of the lots in the section in bulk if 
they want to make sure no one of another faith can be buried in the area.  The city will no 
longer allow a Muslim specific section unless the lots are pre-purchased in bulk.  Bachand also 
went over the current version of our green burial policy so ISVT would be aware of how the city 
intends to hold green/natural burials going forward.  ISTV took information and brought it to 
their board.  They are appreciative of the fact that we’re thinking of them in the design of 
Section 8.  They had a few questions, some of which went to Hayley McClenahan with the city 
attorney’s office.  ISVT asked if there is room for growth in the existing section (where vaults are 
required).  The answer is yes, but 2 of 3 existing trees will need to be removed to make more 
grave space.  This would create 31 more lots.  Beyond that there’s not much more room to 
expand in that corner.   
Bachand shared that ISVT asked if they could receive a bulk/reduced lot price for the new 
natural burial lots in Section 8. Based on the green burial prices that the commission previously
Page 2 of 6 
approved and the location of their mosque (the address they would use as lot owners), ISVT 
would need to pay non-resident rate ($2808 per grave) for all 67 graves totaling over $150,000 
($188,136 to be exact).  ISVT does not have that kind of money available.  They asked for 
forgiveness/leniency and are looking to find a way to make it work.  Bachand explained that the 
67 lots will be available for general public if ISVT doesn’t purchase them all, and that a potential 
option would be to share the space with the general public.  ISVT was vehemently against 
sharing burial space with people of other faiths.   
ISVT proposed putting down a deposit on the 67 graves.  The exact amount has not been 
determined, but the existence of this deposit would allow the city to hold the graves for them.  
Bachand explained that accepting deposits and holding graves is not something we do.  It 
doesn’t matter who the group is or if it’s an individual, we don’t hold graves for anyone.  ISVT is 
still asking that we work with them to try to figure out a way for them to purchase the 67 lots.   
Bachand shared that, in the past, Calvary Nepali Church paid $1000 per lot in 2020.  This was the 
resident rate at the time even though the church is based in Essex).  Temple Sinai purchased lots 
1-42 in Section 7 and paid $200 per lot when lots were $300 to $425 at the time.  We also 
accommodated them with a payment plan, allowing them to pay $5200 up front and $3200 in 
two years.  Temple Sinai later purchased 43 through 48 in Section 7 and paid $1650 for lots or 
$275 per lot. At the time $275 was bond or deed price for lots ($550 was the total lot price).  
Based on this information, it’s clear that the city has worked with other religious groups in the 
past for bulk purchasing.  Bachand intends to offer ISVT all 67 graves at resident rate at his next 
meeting with them in three weeks’ time. 
Diaz share that she felt comfortable giving them some leeway and working with them on a 
payment plan.  She did, however, want to make sure that our contract with them is clear about 
the parameters of when payments are due.  She also felt that the city should get a signed MOU 
from ISVT that includes the payment plan with specific dates.   
Bachand shared that he had reached out to McClenahan and is hoping to meeting with her, Phil, 
and Paul beforehand the next ISVT meeting.  He is working to get the internal details organized 
to make reasonable offer.   
Millar-House shared that she would be interested to hear what McClenahan has to say.  She 
wondered where this offer exist in terms of legal standing, if we should have allowed these 
deals in the past, and if legal was involved in the past. 
Diaz made it clear that she would not be comfortable with this offer if there is not an MOU and 
clear payment plan.  She asked if a vote was needed. 
Bachand did not feel that the commission needed to vote yet.  He would prefer to come to 
commission with a completed plan approved by ISVT and legal rather than to do a partial 
approval from commission now.  He wants to have the Section 8 plan finalized before 
commission votes.
Page 3 of 6 
Mary Wesley agreed with Bachand.  She asked for an update from McClenahan and more 
discussion before any sort of vote takes place. She did make sure that nothing is being held up 
by lack of input from the commission.   
Millar-House asked about the 31 potential lots in the current Muslim section and asked if those 
would be available to the general public as well.   Bachand shared that staff probably wouldn’t 
put the general public in the existing Muslim section because the city portioned that section off 
years ago.  Because it is currently a solely an Islamic burial section we just wouldn’t do that 
internally.  ISVT is always looking for more lots because their population is growing really 
rapidly.  Even with the many new graves we have, ISVT is going to need more lots in just a 
couple of years.  In working through this situation, the city is trying to focus on the issues 
immediately in front of us instead of issues that might come down the line. 
Diaz asked if the only way to get the 31 new graves in the existing section is by taking down the 
trees.  Bachand confirmed that that was the case.  Diaz felt that the city should require an MOU 
for the 31 graves if ISVT decides not to purchase the 67 green lots in Section 8 or and MOU if 
they purchase 67 green lots and then later choose to develop the 31 graves in the existing area.   
Bachand mused that the city could provide ISVT with two options.  With the knowledge that the 
green area will have a ton of restrictions, some members of the muslim community might like to 
be able to choose the hybrid option.   
Diaz shared that she liked the idea of 2 options, however, she did fell that if ISVT chooses the 31 
graves in the existing section the city will not reserve the 67 green burial lots for them.  That 
said, if they choose the 67 green lots, ISVT could still develop the 31 hybrid graves to purchase 
later.   
Bachand explained that part of our plan is, when we bring in the excavator to do site work, the 
city would cut the trees in the existing Muslim section down at the same time.  And in terms of 
not reserving the 67 green graves for them if they choose the 31 hybrid graves, we don’t want 
to give ISVT an ultimatum.  Diaz explained that she felt her proposal was more of an either/or 
option.  She also pointed out that ISVT does not know we intend to remove trees to develop the 
31 hybrid graves.  Bachand felt that we could hold on to the 31 hybrid graves in case they were 
needed in the future. 
McCallum shared that he agrees with the general consensus of the discussion.  He also would 
like to know what legal has to say about these items.  He feels that a payment plan that’s very 
clear in terms of exact dates and amounts would be appropriate given we’ve done one with 
Temple Sinai in the past.  He also wanted to ensure that the city maintains clear boundaries 
regarding religious groups to mitigate any impression of favoritism.   
Bachand appreciated the input as McClenahan will likely need this information.  He will be able 
to tell McClenahan that the commission has verbally agreed to move forward with payment plan 
and MOU as long as it’s legal.
Page 4 of 6 
McCallum added that he’s comfortable with the payment plan/MOU because there is 
precedent.  That said, the commission should have a bulk buying policy in place as well so that 
we don’t end up in this position again.   
Diaz asked if the tree removal in the existing Muslim section would be because we need the 
space to add the graves or would the city plant replacement trees.  She always feels 
disappointed when we have to take trees down without replacing them.  Bachand confirmed 
that we might be able to add more trees to the existing Muslim section.  Generally speaking, we 
can usually find some option for new trees with City Arborist, VJ Comai’s help.  The problem 
with new trees is their roots.  Cemeteries have a love/hate relationship with trees.  From a 
maintenance point of view, we would prefer not to add back trees that we take down, but yes, 
we could replace the removed trees with new ones elsewhere on the grounds. 
 
V. Family Policy Update 
Bachand reminded everyone that he emailed policy to the commissioners and asked what 
questions people have.  He confirmed that the policy was drafted by staff and has been revised 
by legal.  At this juncture, the commission either needs to vote to approve the policy, vote to 
reject the policy, or send the policy back to legal with questions.  The commission has discussed 
this item a lot in previous meetings.   
Diaz shared that she still was of the same mind, that the POA for the deceased should be the 
point person.  Millar-House’s biggest concern was the legal aspect.  She wanted to make sure it 
covers all the bases in terms of the city’s responsibility.   
Bachand confirmed that McClenahan had added language to policy to make sure everything is 
covered.  At this time it is up to the commission to make a decision if they want to go with policy 
or not.  Millar-House felt that since the policy has been approved by legal she’s comfortable 
moving forward. 
Wesley still had some concerns regarding how to carry out policy, but if legal is good with it she 
doesn’t have any concerns or things to add or change.  
McCallum had no questions and was ready to vote affirmatively.  
Diaz felt that she still doesn’t feel like that one person would be able to dictate the burial 
options, but she didn’t have another solution and confirmed she would vote with the majority.   
Bachand asked to put the policy to an official vote. 
Wesley moved to adopt family authorization for interment policy as drafted.  McCallum and 
Millar-House second.  The motion passes.   
Millar-House added that, in terms of Diaz’s concerns, staff should make sure that the language is 
very clear with customers and confirm with them that the form they’re completing is a legal 
document.   
 
VI. Vault Ordinance Update
Page 5 of 6 
Bachand shared the new language that had been revised by legal.  He briefly read through the 
new policy regarding Division 4 - Natural Burial Areas.  This language was revised and written by 
attorneys.  The legalese of the document goes way above Bachand’s head, but he trusts the city 
attorneys that it is written the way it should be.  He noted that this ordinance update is a big 
item for Wesley, Millar-House, and previous commissioner Martha Dallas.  He confirmed that 
the next step is to get commissioner approval on the language change.  
Wesley thanked Bachand and everyone involved for keeping this item moving forward.  She 
asked if the commission would be approving a draft or if this is the final language.  Bachand 
confirmed that changes can still be made.     
Wesley suggested that the commission might put more regulations in the policy based on 
language.  She also pointed out that there should be a difference between what is in the 
ordinances and interdepartmental regulations.  She would prefer to keep the ordinance 
language basic as regulations are more easily flexible than ordinances.  Her thought is that, as 
we learn more and things change, we want to be able to shift to make things work.  The green 
burial sub-committee had suggested something like “regulations as outlined by commission and 
staff will be followed” because it takes the onus off of the public and allows staff/commission to 
have more control.  
Bachand asked that any question, comments, or concerns about this document be sent via email 
with question so he can go over it with McClenahan.   
Millar-House had some confusion about the line on the second page where the document says 
“an ordinance in relation to.” She asked if this was the ordinance or if this section is where the 
ordinance will go.  Bachand confirmed that the document is quite difficult to understand.   
Millar-House asked if the document was the suggested ordinance change that the sub-
committee submitted to the ordinance committee.  Bachand was not sure, but he will check 
with McClenahan.  He thought it would be a good idea to make sure document says exactly 
what it needs to say and is ready to be voted on.  For clarity, again, he confirmed that the 
commission wants to change the vault ordinance to state that every full burial requires a vault 
except in natural burial areas of Lakeview.  He wanted to make sure that the existing document 
does that.   
Wesley shared concerns that the language is too detailed.  Diaz and Millar-House agreed that we 
might not need that level of detail in the ordinances.  Bachand stated that he will share the 
comment that commission has questions about the level of detail in the language with 
McClenahan. 
Wesley wondered if it would be possible to just state who makes the rules in the ordinance, not 
state what the rules themselves are.   
Bachand asked commissioners to email comments and questions to him so he can get the exact 
wording correct when he meets with McClenahan.  He asked that commissioners review the 
policy and share their questions with him in the next few weeks.
Page 6 of 6 
 
VII. Lot Purchase Agreement 
Bachand noted that McClenahan has made some changes to our current document.  These 
changes do not need to be voted on by the commission. He just wanted to let the 
commissioners know that we will be changing to document internally to match McClenahan’s 
preferred language.  This covers the interment policy and is provided to new lot purchasers.   
 
VIII. Cemetery Construction Update 
Bachand shared good news!  The office construction will be completed by the end of the 
October.  SD Ireland said that the paving and walkway have been completed, the seeding is 
done, and all that’s still needed is topsoil and landscaping.  SDI is coming this weekend to do the 
last of the work.  They will also be doing line striping in parking lot.   
Millar-House reminded Bachand about a previous discussion regarding adding native habitat 
plantings as part of the new landscaping.  Bachand confirmed that staff has worked with 
conservation to develop the garden area with native plants.  He also shared that working 
foreman Paul Morris reached out to the foreman from the SDI project and asked them not plant 
any grass seed on embankment.  The plan is to connect to lower section of native plants behind 
the office that’s already been planted. 
 
IX. Adjournment 
Diaz moved to adjourn, Wesley seconded , and the meeting was adjourned by unanimous 
consent at 5:30pm.  The next meeting will be held on November 26 (or a date to be 
determined), 2026 at the Lakeview office and via Zoom.
